_meta.note: Championships are region-level and apply to any event. Pick an event with --event (e.g. 1500m_men). The rankings URL is built from rankings_url_template using the event's discipline + gender. Per-event qualification config (quota, defending champion / auto_invites, optional window override) lives under 'events'. 'data_source' aliases the ranking-list fetch to another championship's cache (same list, different qualification overlay). 'contested_events_only': events absent from 'events' are NOT on this championship's programme (the UI shows 'not_contested_note' for them). short_label / scope_label / rank_label are presentation strings for the UI tabs. A championship may also declare a 'qualification_feed' (WA's own 'road to' feed): where a snapshot exists it overrides quota / auto_invites and supplies 'not_in_field' — the ranked athletes WA doesn't list in the field. See feed.py; the values under 'events' are then the fallback.

world.label: World Ranking
world.note: Global World Athletics ranking (all nations). General-ranking questions only; no quota/qualification.

road_to_birmingham.label: Road to Birmingham (2026 European Athletics Championships)
road_to_birmingham.quota_source: European Athletics 'Qualification System and Entry Standards' (Birmingham 2026), 'Target number of athletes / teams per event' table.
road_to_birmingham.qualification_note: Quota is the TOTAL target field; world rankings only fill what remains after entry-standard achievers, finishing-position qualifiers, the defending-champion wildcard and approved unqualified athletes. This tool treats the field as ranking-only (champion bye + 3-per-country cap), so it over-counts ranking places. Defending champions are the Rome 2024 European Outdoor Champions (wildcard applies only if entered by their federation; some may not compete). 10000m uses an 18-month qualification window.

road_to_ultimate.label: Road to Budapest (2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship)
road_to_ultimate.quota_source: World Athletics 'Road to the Ultimate' qualification feed (getChampionshipQualifications, competition 7212925), refreshed weekly by scripts.refresh_seed: quota = entryNumber, wildcards = the rows WA marks 'Qualified by Wild Card'. The per-event values below are only the fallback when no snapshot is available.
road_to_ultimate.qualification_note: Invitational: wildcards (Olympic champion, World champion, the 2026 Diamond League Final winner, plus any exceptional or host-federation invitation) take the first places and the world rankings fill the rest. NO country cap. Champion wildcards sit inside the base field (16 for the 800m, 12 for the 1500m/5000m); an extra invitation can push the field past it, as in the men's 1500m at 13. Ranked athletes WA doesn't list in the field (declined, injured, contesting another event) take no place, so the real cutoff sits lower than the ranking list implies. Only 26 individual events are contested; the 10000m and 3000m steeplechase are not on the programme.
road_to_ultimate.not_contested_note: This event will not be competed at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship 2026.
road_to_ultimate.qualification_footnote: The 2026 Diamond League Final winner also gets a wildcard — that meet is in Brussels on 4–5 September 2026, so the name appears here once World Athletics adds it to the qualification feed.
road_to_ultimate.not_in_field_note: Greyed rows are ranked athletes World Athletics does not list in the field — declined, injured or contesting another event. They keep their ranking place but take no qualifying place.

qualification_feed._note: WA event ids for getChampionshipQualifications (see feed.py).
